title: Compounding Growth Loops, SEO Engines, and Scaling Beyond Funnels
content:
Lenny Rachitsky: Welcome Casey Winters. Casey was Chief Product Officer at Eventbrite, growth lead at Pinterest and Grubhub, and is a partner at Reforge. Casey, Reforge and yourself fundamentally changed how tech companies view growth by introducing 'Growth Loops' instead of traditional linear funnels. Why are funnels broken?

Casey Winters: The linear marketing funnel—Acquisition -> Activation -> Retention -> Referral -> Revenue—implies that you put money or effort in at the top, lose 90% through the leaky middle, and take a few customers out at the bottom. To get more customers, you have to pour more money into the top. That does not compound. Growth loops, on the other hand, are closed systems where the output of one cycle reinvests as the input of the next cycle.

Lenny Rachitsky: Can you give an example of a great organic growth loop?

Casey Winters: Look at Pinterest or Eventbrite. At Pinterest: A user signs up -> they discover content and pin an image to a public board -> Google indexes that pin -> a new searcher searches for that topic on Google -> they discover the pinned page -> they sign up. That is a User-Generated Content (UGC) SEO loop. At Eventbrite: An event organizer creates an event -> they invite 100 attendees -> those 100 attendees experience the ticket booking interface -> 2 of them are also organizers who decide to host their own event on Eventbrite. That is a viral product loop. When your loops operate autonomously, your CAC drops toward zero.
